thread.title: Apple discloses minor self-driving crash in California - MarketWatch

author: Max A. Cherney
title: Apple discloses minor self-driving crash in California - MarketWatch
text:
Apple Inc. AAPL, +1.16% revealed that one of its self-driving test vehicles was involved in a minor crash in Sunnyvale, Calif. In a filing with the California Department of Motor Vehicles, the company said that a Nissan Leaf rear-ended the Apple self-driving test car, a Lexus RX 450h, while it was attempting to merge onto the Lawrence Expressway. According to the DMV document, the Apple car was in autonomous mode and traveling less than 1 mph while attempt to merge. The Leaf struck the Apple car at roughly 15 mph; there was damage to both cars and no injuries, according to the document. The collision occurred Aug. 24 at around 2:58 p.m. local time. Apple stock was up 0.1% after hours and closed up 1.2% to $227.63 during the regular session. The S&P 500 index SPX, +0.01% rose less than 0.1% Friday. The Dow Jones Industrial Average DJIA, -0.09% of which Apple is a component, closed down less than 0.1%.
